# Single CI pipeline for this repository.
#
# Replaces .github/workflows/build.yml and run-ui-tests.yml, and the four
# separate Buildkite pipelines they were first migrated to. One pipeline means
# one GitHub webhook and one place to configure triggers; variation is
# expressed with `if:` below rather than by duplicating pipeline settings.
#
# Two things deliberately stay on GitHub Actions, both for the same reason —
# they need to launch a full Android Studio, and these agents are 2 vCPU / 4 GB:
#
#   .github/workflows/qodana_code_quality.yml
#     Performs a full Gradle project import, which makes the IntelliJ Platform
#     Gradle Plugin unpack the whole Android Studio distribution alongside
#     Qodana's own analyzer JVM.
#
#   .github/workflows/release.yml
#     `publishPlugin` pulls in `buildSearchableOptions`, which starts an IDE to
#     generate the marketplace search index. A Publish Plugin step lived here
#     briefly and was reverted: build 92 died in `buildSearchableOptions` with
#     "Gradle build daemon disappeared unexpectedly", the OOM signature
#     described in gradle/ci.properties. Excluding the task would have fixed
#     the build at the cost of shipping releases without their search index —
#     GitHub's runners have the memory, so publishing went back there instead.
#     That workflow triggers on the GitHub `release` event, so the draft below
#     is what connects the two halves: Buildkite drafts it, you publish it,
#     GitHub Actions ships it.
#
# What runs when:
#   branch push / PR   build, test, verify
#   push to main       ...plus a GitHub release draft
#   manual             UI tests, when started with RUN_UI_TESTS=true:
#                        bk build create -e RUN_UI_TESTS=true
#
# The pipeline must have build_branches and build_pull_requests enabled for
# these conditions to be reachable. Tag builds no longer do anything here; if
# build_tags is left on, a tag push just re-runs build/test/verify.

steps:
  - label: ":hammer: Build"
    key: build
    # buildSearchableOptions launches a full IntelliJ IDE and needs ~4GB. It only
    # generates marketplace search indexes, so it is skipped on CI.
    command: "gradle buildPlugin -x buildSearchableOptions"
    plugins: &gradle_docker
      - docker#v5.12.0:
          image: "gradle:9-jdk21"
          mount-buildkite-agent: true
    artifact_paths:
      - "build/distributions/*.zip"

  - label: ":test_tube: Test"
    key: test
    # Same three-JVM squeeze that used to kill Verify: Gradle daemon, Kotlin
    # daemon and the forked test JVM. This step passed in build 58 and was
    # OOM-killed in 59 and 61, so it sits right on the limit. The memory
    # settings come from gradle/ci.properties.
    commands:
      - &apply_ci_gradle_properties |
        # Gradle natively reads $$GRADLE_USER_HOME/gradle.properties, and values
        # there take precedence over the project's own gradle.properties.
        # Appending is how the CI-only file gets loaded without editing anything
        # tracked in the repo, and without affecting local builds.
        GUH="$${GRADLE_USER_HOME:-$$HOME/.gradle}"
        mkdir -p "$$GUH"
        cat gradle/ci.properties >> "$$GUH/gradle.properties"
        echo "--- CI Gradle properties applied ---"
        grep -vE '^\s*(#|$$)' gradle/ci.properties
      - gradle check --no-daemon --max-workers 1
    plugins: *gradle_docker
    artifact_paths:
      - "build/reports/tests/**/*"

  - label: ":shield: Verify Plugin"
    key: verify
    depends_on: build
    plugins: *gradle_docker
    commands:
      - *apply_ci_gradle_properties
      - buildkite-agent artifact download "build/distributions/*.zip" .
      - |
        # Reuse the artifact the Build step produced instead of recompiling.
        # buildPlugin's archiveFile — which is what verifyPlugin's own
        # archiveFile defaults to — resolves to build/distributions/<name>-<version>.zip,
        # exactly where the download above lands. So excluding buildPlugin is
        # safe: the @InputFile already exists at the path the convention points
        # to, and Gradle only needs it present at execution time.
        #
        # Skipping the rebuild is what keeps this step inside the agent's memory:
        # no compile means no Kotlin daemon, so only the Gradle daemon and the
        # forked verifier are live. Three JVMs at once is what used to exhaust
        # the agent and surface as "Gradle build daemon disappeared unexpectedly".
        ls -la build/distributions/

        gradle verifyPlugin \
          -x buildPlugin \
          -x buildSearchableOptions \
          --no-daemon --max-workers 1
    artifact_paths:
      - "build/reports/pluginVerifier/**/*"

  # Replaces .github/workflows/run-ui-tests.yml, which was workflow_dispatch only.
  # Start with: bk build create -e RUN_UI_TESTS=true
  #
  # WARNING: this cannot pass yet. There is no `runIdeForUiTests` task — IntelliJ
  # Platform Gradle Plugin 2.x renamed it to `testIdeUi`, which additionally
  # requires testFramework(TestFrameworkType.Starter) and intellij-ui-test-robot.
  # build.gradle.kts currently declares TestFrameworkType.Platform only.
  #
  # Linux only: the sole hosted queue is linux/amd64, so the macOS and Windows
  # legs of the original matrix had no agents to run on.
  - label: ":linux: UI Tests"
    key: ui-tests
    if: build.env("RUN_UI_TESTS") == "true"
    env:
      DISPLAY: ":99.0"
    plugins:
      - docker#v5.12.0:
          image: "gradle:9-jdk21"
          mount-buildkite-agent: true
          environment:
            - DISPLAY
    commands:
      # The gradle image is Debian-based and runs as root; Xvfb is not included.
      - apt-get update -qq && apt-get install -y -qq xvfb curl
      - Xvfb -ac :99 -screen 0 1920x1080x16 &
      - gradle runIdeForUiTests --no-daemon --max-workers 1 &
      - |
        # Wait for the IDE's robot-server (replaces url-health-check-action)
        for i in $$(seq 1 15); do
          if curl -sf http://127.0.0.1:8082 > /dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo "IDE is ready"
            break
          fi
          echo "Attempt $$i/15 — waiting 30s..."
          sleep 30
        done
      - gradle test --no-daemon --max-workers 1
    artifact_paths:
      - "build/reports/tests/**/*"

  # ─── Release draft, once CI is green on main ───────────────────────────────
  #
  # The handoff to .github/workflows/release.yml: this drafts the release, you
  # publish it, and publishing fires the GitHub `release` event that workflow
  # listens for.
  - label: ":github: Create Release Draft"
    key: release-draft
    # `if` and `branches` are mutually exclusive on a step, so the branch
    # restriction lives in the condition.
    if: build.branch == "main"
    depends_on:
      - test
      - verify
    plugins: *gradle_docker
    commands:
      - apt-get update -qq && apt-get install -y -qq gh
      - |
        # Assign and export separately. `export VAR="$$(cmd)"` reports the exit
        # status of `export`, not of the command substitution, so a failed
        # secret read would silently yield an empty token and surface much
        # later as a confusing gh error.
        GITHUB_TOKEN="$$(buildkite-agent secret get GITHUB_TOKEN)"
        export GITHUB_TOKEN

        PROPERTIES="$$(gradle properties --console=plain -q)"
        VERSION="$$(echo "$$PROPERTIES" | grep "^version:" | cut -f2- -d ' ')"
        CHANGELOG="$$(gradle getChangelog --unreleased --no-header --console=plain -q)"

        gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/releases \
          --jq '.[] | select(.draft == true) | .id' \
          | xargs -I '{}' gh api -X DELETE repos/{owner}/{repo}/releases/{}

        # gh prints the new release's URL on stdout. A draft has no tag yet, so
        # that URL is the only way back to it — hence the annotation rather than
        # leaving it buried in the job log.
        RELEASE_URL="$$(gh release create "v$$VERSION" \
          --draft \
          --title "v$$VERSION" \
          --notes "$$CHANGELOG")"

        buildkite-agent annotate \
          "Release draft [**v$$VERSION**]($$RELEASE_URL) is ready to review and publish." \
          --style success \
          --context release-draft
hec

toolUseResult.originalFile:
# Buildkite CI

One pipeline, `aapv`, in the `z8dn` org. Its only stored step is
`buildkite-agent pipeline upload .buildkite/pipeline.yml` — every real step comes
from that file at the commit being built, so pipeline changes are reviewed like
any other code.

Deliberately **one** pipeline, not one per workflow. Each Buildkite pipeline
needs its own GitHub webhook; the migration started with four and three never
had one, so they never ran. Express variation with `if:` on steps instead of
adding pipelines. If a step never fires, check
`gh api repos/z8dn/advanced-android-project-view/hooks` against the pipeline's
`provider.webhook_url` before anything else.

| Trigger | Runs |
|---|---|
| branch push / PR | build, test, verify |
| push to main | ...plus the release draft |
| tag push | publish to JetBrains Marketplace, nothing else |
| manual, `RUN_UI_TESTS=true` | UI tests |

**Qodana is not here.** It stays on GitHub Actions — see the root `CLAUDE.md`.

## Agents

A single hosted queue, `default`: `LINUX_AMD64_2X4` — 2 vCPU, 4 GB, linux/amd64
only. There are no macOS or Windows agents, which is why the UI test matrix was
reduced to Linux.

Memory is the binding constraint on nearly everything here. When a step dies
with no useful stack trace, suspect the agent before suspecting Gradle.

## Gotchas

These each cost real debugging time:

- **Cluster secrets are not in the job environment.** Read them with
  `buildkite-agent secret get KEY`. YAML written as `$${SOME_TOKEN?}` never
  resolves, even when the secret exists. A missing secret gives a clean
  `404 Secret not found`, not a syntax error.
- **`if:` and `branches:` are mutually exclusive** on a step. Put the branch
  restriction inside the condition.
- **A step skipped by `if:` shows as `broken`** — that means "filtered out", not
  "failed". Publish, UI Tests and Release Draft are `broken` on an ordinary
  branch build, and that is correct.
- **`buildkite-agent` is not inside the docker plugin's container** unless the
  step sets `mount-buildkite-agent: true`. Needed for artifact download and
  secret reads.
- **Buildkite interpolates single-`$` variables at upload time**, including
  inside comments. Use `$$` for anything the shell should see.
- **Hosted agent instance shape cannot be changed via the REST API.** `PATCH`
  silently ignores a `hosted_agents` body and returns the old shape;
  `bk queue update` only exposes `--description` and `--retry-agent-affinity`.
  Use the web UI. Renaming a pipeline *does* work via PATCH and preserves the
  webhook URL.
- **The `bk` CLI keeps its token in the macOS keychain**, so under a sandbox
  every REST call returns 401 even though `~/.config/bk.yaml` looks configured.

## Memory design

Two decisions keep this inside 4 GB. Do not undo either while the agents are
this size.

**Verify reuses Build's artifact rather than recompiling.** Build uploads the
plugin zip; Verify downloads it and runs `gradle verifyPlugin -x buildPlugin`.
That works with no build-script support because `verifyPlugin.archiveFile`
defaults to `buildPlugin.archiveFile`, which resolves to
`build/distributions/<name>-<version>.zip` — exactly where the download lands,
and Gradle only needs the input present at execution time. Skipping the rebuild
means no Kotlin daemon, which is what used to push the step over the limit.

**CI-only Gradle settings live in `gradle/ci.properties`**, appended to
`$GRADLE_USER_HOME/gradle.properties` where Gradle reads it natively and it
outranks the project's own file. Local builds never load it. See that file for
why each value is what it is.

If the verifier ever needs more heap, note it is a `JavaExec`, so use
`tasks.verifyPlugin { maxHeapSize = ... }` — **never**
`intellijPlatform.pluginVerification.freeArgs`, whose contents go to the
verifier's CLI rather than the JVM and corrupt the argument list.

## Useful commands

```bash
bk build view -p aapv                       # most recent build on this branch
bk build list -p aapv                       # recent builds
bk build create -p aapv -e RUN_UI_TESTS=true # run the UI test step
bk secret list --cluster-uuid <uuid>        # what secrets exist
```

# Buildkite CI

One pipeline, `aapv`, in the `z8dn` org. Its only stored step is
`buildkite-agent pipeline upload .buildkite/pipeline.yml` — every real step comes
from that file at the commit being built, so pipeline changes are reviewed like
any other code.

Deliberately **one** pipeline, not one per workflow. Each Buildkite pipeline
needs its own GitHub webhook; the migration started with four and three never
had one, so they never ran. Express variation with `if:` on steps instead of
adding pipelines. If a step never fires, check
`gh api repos/z8dn/advanced-android-project-view/hooks` against the pipeline's
`provider.webhook_url` before anything else.

| Trigger | Runs |
|---|---|
| branch push / PR | build, test, verify |
| push to main | ...plus the release draft |
| manual, `RUN_UI_TESTS=true` | UI tests |

**Qodana and publishing are not here.** Both stay on GitHub Actions, for the
same reason: each needs to launch a full Android Studio, which does not fit in
4 GB. See the root `CLAUDE.md`.

A Publish Plugin step did live here briefly and was reverted. `publishPlugin`
pulls in `buildSearchableOptions`, which starts an IDE to build the marketplace
search index; build 92 died in that task with `Gradle build daemon disappeared
unexpectedly`. `-x buildSearchableOptions` would have made it pass, but every
published release would then ship without its search index. Don't re-add it
while the agents are this size.

Releasing is therefore a handoff: Buildkite drafts the release on `main`, you
publish the draft, and publishing fires the GitHub `release` event that
`.github/workflows/release.yml` listens for. Nothing here keys off tags.

## Agents

A single hosted queue, `default`: `LINUX_AMD64_2X4` — 2 vCPU, 4 GB, linux/amd64
only. There are no macOS or Windows agents, which is why the UI test matrix was
reduced to Linux.

Memory is the binding constraint on nearly everything here. When a step dies
with no useful stack trace, suspect the agent before suspecting Gradle.

## Gotchas

These each cost real debugging time:

- **Cluster secrets are not in the job environment.** Read them with
  `buildkite-agent secret get KEY`. YAML written as `$${SOME_TOKEN?}` never
  resolves, even when the secret exists. A missing secret gives a clean
  `404 Secret not found`, not a syntax error.
- **`if:` and `branches:` are mutually exclusive** on a step. Put the branch
  restriction inside the condition.
- **A step skipped by `if:` shows as `broken`** — that means "filtered out", not
  "failed". Publish, UI Tests and Release Draft are `broken` on an ordinary
  branch build, and that is correct.
- **`buildkite-agent` is not inside the docker plugin's container** unless the
  step sets `mount-buildkite-agent: true`. Needed for artifact download and
  secret reads.
- **Buildkite interpolates single-`$` variables at upload time**, including
  inside comments. Use `$$` for anything the shell should see.
- **Hosted agent instance shape cannot be changed via the REST API.** `PATCH`
  silently ignores a `hosted_agents` body and returns the old shape;
  `bk queue update` only exposes `--description` and `--retry-agent-affinity`.
  Use the web UI. Renaming a pipeline *does* work via PATCH and preserves the
  webhook URL.
- **The `bk` CLI keeps its token in the macOS keychain**, so under a sandbox
  every REST call returns 401 even though `~/.config/bk.yaml` looks configured.

## Memory design

Two decisions keep this inside 4 GB. Do not undo either while the agents are
this size.

**Verify reuses Build's artifact rather than recompiling.** Build uploads the
plugin zip; Verify downloads it and runs `gradle verifyPlugin -x buildPlugin`.
That works with no build-script support because `verifyPlugin.archiveFile`
defaults to `buildPlugin.archiveFile`, which resolves to
`build/distributions/<name>-<version>.zip` — exactly where the download lands,
and Gradle only needs the input present at execution time. Skipping the rebuild
means no Kotlin daemon, which is what used to push the step over the limit.

**CI-only Gradle settings live in `gradle/ci.properties`**, appended to
`$GRADLE_USER_HOME/gradle.properties` where Gradle reads it natively and it
outranks the project's own file. Local builds never load it. See that file for
why each value is what it is.

If the verifier ever needs more heap, note it is a `JavaExec`, so use
`tasks.verifyPlugin { maxHeapSize = ... }` — **never**
`intellijPlatform.pluginVerification.freeArgs`, whose contents go to the
verifier's CLI rather than the JVM and corrupt the argument list.

## Useful commands

```bash
bk build view -p aapv                       # most recent build on this branch
bk build list -p aapv                       # recent builds
bk build create -p aapv -e RUN_UI_TESTS=true # run the UI test step
bk secret list --cluster-uuid <uuid>        # what secrets exist
```

`6069f2e4-0dae-42b5-ada6-36a76366d092`.

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## Project Overview

**Advanced Android Project Tree (A2PT)** is an IntelliJ Platform plugin for Android Studio that enhances the Android Project View with customizable file grouping and build directory visibility.

## Common Commands

```bash
./gradlew build              # Full build with all checks
./gradlew buildPlugin        # Build the plugin distribution ZIP
./gradlew runIde             # Run plugin in a development Android Studio instance
./gradlew test               # Run unit tests
./gradlew check              # Run all tests and code inspections
./gradlew verifyPlugin       # Run plugin structure verification
./gradlew runPluginVerifier  # Run plugin verification on targeted IDEs
```

## Architecture

The plugin intercepts IntelliJ's project tree via extension points and injects custom nodes.

**Package:** `com.z8dn.plugins.a2pt`

### Key Extension Points (registered in `plugin.xml`)
- `treeStructureProvider` — intercepts and modifies the Android Project View tree
- `androidViewNodeProvider` — extends Android module nodes with custom children
- `applicationService` — `AndroidViewSettings` for persistent state
- `applicationConfigurable` — settings UI under Tools menu
- `postStartupActivity` — refreshes view on project open
- `searchScopesProvider` — exposes file groups as Find/Replace scopes

### Source Layout
- `actions/` — toggle actions for build dir and module-level file display
- `nodes/` — custom tree node classes (`ProjectFileGroupNode`, `ProjectFileNode`, `GradleModuleWithProjectFiles`)
- `providers/` — tree structure providers that inject nodes (`AdvancedAndroidViewProvider`, `CustomNonAndroidNodeProvider`, `ProjectFilesTreeStructureProvider`)
- `settings/` — `AndroidViewSettings` (PersistentStateComponent), configurable UI, and group dialog
- `scopes/` — `ProjectFileGroupScopeProvider` for search scope integration
- `utils/` — file matching (`AndroidViewNodeUtils`) and display formatting (`ProjectFileDisplayUtils`)

### Data Flow
1. User toggles features via actions → stored in `AndroidViewSettings` (persisted as `androidViewSettings.xml`)
2. Tree providers read settings and intercept the tree to inject custom nodes
3. File matching uses glob patterns and case-insensitive matching via `PatternMatcher`
4. Two display modes: files under each module (`showProjectFilesInModule=true`) or grouped at project root

### Key Settings
- `showBuildDirectory` — show/hide `build/` directories in the tree
- `showProjectFilesInModule` — toggle between module-level and project-root grouping
- `projectFileGroups` — list of `ProjectFileGroup` objects (name + glob patterns)

## CI

CI is a deliberate hybrid, not a single system:

- **Buildkite** runs build, test, verify, release draft, publish and UI tests, as
  one pipeline defined in `.buildkite/pipeline.yml`. See `.buildkite/CLAUDE.md`
  before changing anything there — the memory constraints and step conditions
  are not obvious from the YAML alone.
- **GitHub Actions** runs Qodana only (`.github/workflows/qodana_code_quality.yml`).
  It stays there because Qodana performs a full Gradle project import, which
  makes the IntelliJ Platform Gradle Plugin unpack the whole Android Studio
  distribution next to Qodana's own analyzer JVM. That needs far more memory
  than the Buildkite agents have, and GitHub's runners provide it free.

One pinned version looks wrong and is not:

- `qodana-action@v2026.2` drives `linter: jetbrains/qodana-jvm-community:2025.3`.
  The mismatch is intentional. Older actions fail Gradle import with
  `Invalid Gradle JDK configuration found`; bumping the linter to match the
  action also fails. This pairing is the one that works.

`.idea/gradle.xml` used to pin `gradleJvm` to `jbr-17` while the project
targeted 21. That pin was never the cause of the error above — Qodana passed
with it either way — so it now tracks the toolchain at `jbr-21`.

CI-only Gradle settings belong in `gradle/ci.properties`, never in
`gradle.properties`, so local builds keep their own tuning.

## Dependencies & Compatibility
- Kotlin 2.4.10, JDK 21
- IntelliJ Platform Gradle Plugin 2.18.1
- Target: Android Studio Quail 3 (2026.1.3.7) and later, `pluginSinceBuild = 261`
- Bundled plugins used: `com.intellij.gradle`, `org.jetbrains.android`, `com.intellij.java`
- No external runtime dependencies

## Commit Conventions
Follow Conventional Commits: `feat:`, `fix:`, `docs:`, `chore:`, `refactor:`, `test:`, `ci:`

Reverts the Publish Plugin step from Buildkite and restores `.github/workflows/release.yml`.

## Why

The Buildkite publish step could never have worked on the hosted agents. `publishPlugin` pulls in `buildSearchableOptions`, which starts a full Android Studio to generate the marketplace search index. [Build 92](https://buildkite.com/z8dn/aapv/builds/92) — the first tag build since the migration — died in exactly that task:

```
> Task :compileKotlin
> Task :buildSearchableOptions

FAILURE: Build failed with an exception.
* What went wrong:
Gradle build daemon disappeared unexpectedly (it may have been killed or may have crashed)
```

That message is the OOM signature documented in `gradle/ci.properties`. `-x buildSearchableOptions` would have made the step green at the cost of shipping every release without its search index. GitHub's runners have the memory for free on a public repo — already the reason Qodana stays there — so publishing goes back to the same place.

`release.yml` is restored byte-identical to its pre-migration version. Its four signing secrets (`PUBLISH_TOKEN`, `CERTIFICATE_CHAIN`, `PRIVATE_KEY`, `PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD`) were never removed from the repository, so it works as-is.

Buildkite drafts the GitHub release on every green `main` build → you publish the draft → publishing fires the `release` event → `release.yml` signs and ships to JetBrains Marketplace.

- `diff <(git show 4dd081e^:.github/workflows/release.yml) .github/workflows/release.yml` → identical

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## Project Overview

**Advanced Android Project Tree (A2PT)** is an IntelliJ Platform plugin for Android Studio that enhances the Android Project View with customizable file grouping and build directory visibility.

## Common Commands

```bash
./gradlew build              # Full build with all checks
./gradlew buildPlugin        # Build the plugin distribution ZIP
./gradlew runIde             # Run plugin in a development Android Studio instance
./gradlew test               # Run unit tests
./gradlew check              # Run all tests and code inspections
./gradlew verifyPlugin       # Run plugin structure verification
./gradlew runPluginVerifier  # Run plugin verification on targeted IDEs
```

## Architecture

The plugin intercepts IntelliJ's project tree via extension points and injects custom nodes.

**Package:** `com.z8dn.plugins.a2pt`

### Key Extension Points (registered in `plugin.xml`)
- `treeStructureProvider` — intercepts and modifies the Android Project View tree
- `androidViewNodeProvider` — extends Android module nodes with custom children
- `applicationService` — `AndroidViewSettings` for persistent state
- `applicationConfigurable` — settings UI under Tools menu
- `postStartupActivity` — refreshes view on project open
- `searchScopesProvider` — exposes file groups as Find/Replace scopes

### Source Layout
- `actions/` — toggle actions for build dir and module-level file display
- `nodes/` — custom tree node classes (`ProjectFileGroupNode`, `ProjectFileNode`, `GradleModuleWithProjectFiles`)
- `providers/` — tree structure providers that inject nodes (`AdvancedAndroidViewProvider`, `CustomNonAndroidNodeProvider`, `ProjectFilesTreeStructureProvider`)
- `settings/` — `AndroidViewSettings` (PersistentStateComponent), configurable UI, and group dialog
- `scopes/` — `ProjectFileGroupScopeProvider` for search scope integration
- `utils/` — file matching (`AndroidViewNodeUtils`) and display formatting (`ProjectFileDisplayUtils`)

### Data Flow
1. User toggles features via actions → stored in `AndroidViewSettings` (persisted as `androidViewSettings.xml`)
2. Tree providers read settings and intercept the tree to inject custom nodes
3. File matching uses glob patterns and case-insensitive matching via `PatternMatcher`
4. Two display modes: files under each module (`showProjectFilesInModule=true`) or grouped at project root

### Key Settings
- `showBuildDirectory` — show/hide `build/` directories in the tree
- `showProjectFilesInModule` — toggle between module-level and project-root grouping
- `projectFileGroups` — list of `ProjectFileGroup` objects (name + glob patterns)

## CI

CI is a deliberate hybrid, not a single system:

- **Buildkite** runs build, test, verify, release draft, publish and UI tests, as
  one pipeline defined in `.buildkite/pipeline.yml`. See `.buildkite/CLAUDE.md`
  before changing anything there — the memory constraints and step conditions
  are not obvious from the YAML alone.
- **GitHub Actions** runs Qodana only (`.github/workflows/qodana_code_quality.yml`).
  It stays there because Qodana performs a full Gradle project import, which
  makes the IntelliJ Platform Gradle Plugin unpack the whole Android Studio
  distribution next to Qodana's own analyzer JVM. That needs far more memory
  than the Buildkite agents have, and GitHub's runners provide it free.

One pinned version looks wrong and is not:

- `qodana-action@v2026.2` drives `linter: jetbrains/qodana-jvm-community:2025.3`.
  The mismatch is intentional. Older actions fail Gradle import with
  `Invalid Gradle JDK configuration found`; bumping the linter to match the
  action also fails. This pairing is the one that works.

`.idea/gradle.xml` used to pin `gradleJvm` to `jbr-17` while the project
targeted 21. That pin was never the cause of the error above — Qodana passed
with it either way — so it now tracks the toolchain at `jbr-21`.

CI-only Gradle settings belong in `gradle/ci.properties`, never in
`gradle.properties`, so local builds keep their own tuning.

## Dependencies & Compatibility
- Kotlin 2.4.10, JDK 21
- IntelliJ Platform Gradle Plugin 2.18.1
- Target: Android Studio Quail 3 (2026.1.3.7) and later, `pluginSinceBuild = 261`
- Bundled plugins used: `com.intellij.gradle`, `org.jetbrains.android`, `com.intellij.java`
- No external runtime dependencies

## Commit Conventions
Follow Conventional Commits: `feat:`, `fix:`, `docs:`, `chore:`, `refactor:`, `test:`, `ci:`

Reverts the CI topology introduced by #48. Supersedes #66, which moved only the publish step.

## Why

The free plan's hosted agents are 2 vCPU / 4 GB, and too much of this build needs more:

- **Qodana** does a full Gradle project import, which makes the IntelliJ Platform Gradle Plugin unpack the whole Android Studio distribution next to Qodana's own analyzer JVM. It never moved off GHA for this reason.
- **`publishPlugin`** pulls in `buildSearchableOptions`, which starts an IDE to generate the marketplace search index. [Build 92](https://buildkite.com/z8dn/aapv/builds/92) died there with `Gradle build daemon disappeared unexpectedly`. That is what #66 addressed.
- **`buildPlugin`** hits the same task, which is why the Buildkite Build step ran `-x buildSearchableOptions`. Fitting into 4 GB therefore cost real fidelity: a release built there ships without its search index.

GitHub's runners have the memory free on a public repo.

## What this does

Restored verbatim from `4dd081e^`:

| File | Trigger |
|---|---|
| `.github/workflows/build.yml` | push, PR → build, test, verify, release draft |
| `.github/workflows/release.yml` | `release` event → sign, publish to Marketplace, changelog PR |
| `.github/workflows/run-ui-tests.yml` | `workflow_dispatch` → UI tests |

Removed `.buildkite/`, `gradle/ci.properties`, and the `build.gradle.kts` `test` block that existed only to read `testMaxHeapSize` from it. `CLAUDE.md`'s CI section now describes the all-GHA setup and records why Buildkite was tried and dropped.

## Deliberately NOT reverted

`git revert -m 1 4dd081e` would have broken the build. Three changes from #48 are load-bearing:

- `platformType = AI` in `gradle.properties` — read by `pluginVerification` in `build.gradle.kts:120`
- `gradleVersion` — since bumped to 9.7.0 by `91defab`
- `qodana-action@v2026.2` — the pairing proven to work against linter 2025.3; older actions fail Gradle import with `Invalid Gradle JDK configuration found`

## Verification

- All four workflow files parse; jobs are `build/test/verify/releaseDraft`, `release`, `testUI`, `qodana`
- No `buildkite` / `ci.properties` / `testMaxHeapSize` references remain outside the one historical note in `CLAUDE.md`
- All GHA secrets these workflows need (`PUBLISH_TOKEN`, `CERTIFICATE_CHAIN`, `PRIVATE_KEY`, `PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD`, `QODANA_TOKEN_*`) are still in the repo — nothing to re-provision

## Note

`run-ui-tests.yml` is restored as it was, including a pre-existing defect: it calls `runIdeForUiTests`, which IntelliJ Platform Gradle Plugin 2.x renamed to `testIdeUi`, and needs `TestFrameworkType.Starter` + `intellij-ui-test-robot` that `build.gradle.kts` does not declare. It is `workflow_dispatch`-only, so nothing runs it by accident. Predates the migration; out of scope here.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -3

content.content:
1	---
2	name: a2pt-ci-memory-constraints
3	description: "Why A2PT's CI hit OOM and how the artifact-reuse design fixed it without a bigger agent"
4	metadata: 
5	  node_type: memory
6	  type: project
7	  originSessionId: b6074e5e-37c1-4036-af97-73d227a984c2
8	  modified: 2026-08-08T14:07:30.045Z
9	---
10	
11	CI failures on this plugin used to trace back to agent RAM rather than to the code. The symptom is `Gradle build daemon disappeared unexpectedly` — that is the OOM killer, not a Gradle bug.
12	
13	The cause was three JVMs alive at once in the verify step, against a 4 GB agent:
14	
15	- Gradle daemon — `org.gradle.jvmargs=-Xmx2048m -XX:MaxMetaspaceSize=512m` (~2.8 GB)
16	- Kotlin daemon — `kotlin.daemon.jvmargs=-Xmx2048m` (~2.3 GB)
17	- the forked plugin verifier (~1.2 GB)
18	
19	**Resolved 2026-08-08 by not rebuilding.** CI downloads the Build step's artifact and runs `gradle verifyPlugin -x buildPlugin`. No compile, no Kotlin daemon: the step dropped to **2 actionable tasks, 1m43s**, and passes on the unchanged 4 GB agent. Upgrading the agent was considered and proved unnecessary.
20	
21	Excluding `buildPlugin` is safe with no build-script support, because `verifyPlugin.archiveFile` is an `@InputFile` whose convention is `buildPlugin.archiveFile` — which resolves to `build/distributions/<name>-<version>.zip`, exactly where `buildkite-agent artifact download` lands it. Gradle only needs the input present at execution time. (An explicit `-PverifyArchive` override was tried and then reverted as unnecessary; `build.gradle.kts` has no `verifyPlugin` block.)
22	
23	If the verifier ever needs more heap, note it is a `JavaExec`, so use `tasks.verifyPlugin { maxHeapSize = ... }`. **Never `intellijPlatform.pluginVerification.freeArgs`** — those are appended to the verifier's own CLI arguments rather than the JVM's, which is why `0f11d0b` had to be reverted in `4f257bd`.
24	
25	The **Test** step had the same shape (Gradle daemon + Kotlin daemon + forked test JVM) and failed intermittently — passing in 58, OOM-killed in 59 and 61, passing in 60, 62 and 63.
26	
27	**All CI memory tuning lives in `gradle/ci.properties`**, which `.buildkite/pipeline.yml` appends to `$GRADLE_USER_HOME/gradle.properties` — Gradle reads that natively and it takes precedence over the project's own file, so local builds are untouched. It sets `org.gradle.jvmargs`, `kotlin.compiler.execution.strategy=in-process`, and `testMaxHeapSize`.
28	
29	Two things not to undo:
30	
31	- **`testMaxHeapSize` is not redundant with the JVM default.** The docker plugin sets no container memory limit, so ergonomics sizes the heap from what it detects rather than the agent's 4 GB and starves the daemon beside it. Removing it failed twice. `build.gradle.kts` needs one opt-in line to read it, because a task's `maxHeapSize` has no `gradle.properties` equivalent.
32	- **`in-process` is the highest-leverage setting** — it removes the separate Kotlin daemon entirely.
33	
34	The **Build** step has a similar profile but has never failed, so it is deliberately left alone.
35	
36	**Qodana does not fit here at all** and deliberately stays on GitHub Actions (`.github/workflows/qodana_code_quality.yml`). It runs a full Gradle project import, so IJPGP unpacks the whole Android Studio distribution inside the container next to Qodana's analyzer JVM; it was killed with exit 137 even at `-Xmx2500m`. Never cap it with `_JAVA_OPTIONS` — that is inherited by *every* JVM in the container, including the Gradle daemon doing the import, which makes things worse.
37	
38	`buildSearchableOptions` remains excluded on CI — it launches a full IDE and wants ~4 GB on its own.
39	
40	**Why:** `gradle.properties` is tuned for a developer laptop and gives no hint that CI has a quarter of that memory.
41	
42	**How to apply:** when a CI step dies with no useful stack trace, suspect memory, and prefer removing duplicated work over raising heaps or agent size. See [[buildkite-ci-topology]] for the agent shape.
43

- the forked plugin verifier (~1.2 GB)

Gradle only needs the input present at execution time. (An explicit `-PverifyArchive` override was tried and then reverted as unnecessary; `build.gradle.kts` has no `verifyPlugin` block.)

If the verifier ever needs more heap, note it is a `JavaExec`, so use `tasks.verifyPlugin { maxHeapSize = ... }`. **Never `intellijPlatform.pluginVerification.freeArgs`** — those are appended to the verifier's own CLI arguments rather than the JVM's, which is why `0f11d0b` had to be reverted in `4f257bd`.

The **Test** step had the same shape (Gradle daemon + Kotlin daemon + forked test JVM) and failed intermittently — passing in 58, OOM-killed in 59 and 61, passing in 60, 62 and 63.

**All CI memory tuning lives in `gradle/ci.properties`**, which `.buildkite/pipeline.yml` appends to `$GRADLE_USER_HOME/gradle.properties` — Gradle reads that natively and it takes precedence over the project's own file, so local builds are untouched. - **`testMaxHeapSize` is not redundant with the JVM default.** The docker plugin sets no container memory limit, so ergonomics sizes the heap from what it detects rather than the agent's 4 GB and starves the daemon beside it. - **`in-process` is the highest-leverage setting** — it removes the separate Kotlin daemon entirely.

The **Build** step has a similar profile but has never failed, so it is deliberately left alone.

**Qodana does not fit here at all** and deliberately stays on GitHub Actions (`.github/workflows/qodana_code_quality.yml`). It runs a full Gradle project import, so IJPGP unpacks the whole Android Studio distribution inside the container next to Qodana's analyzer JVM; it was killed with exit 137 even at `-Xmx2500m`. Never cap it with `_JAVA_OPTIONS` — that is inherited by *every* JVM in the container, including the Gradle daemon doing the import, which makes things worse.

`buildSearchableOptions` remains excluded on CI — it launches a full IDE and wants ~4 GB on its own.

- **`publishPlugin` OOM-killed on the first real tag build** (build 92), dying in `buildSearchableOptions`, which starts an IDE to generate the marketplace search index. Reverted to GHA in PR #66.
- **`buildPlugin` hits the same task**, which is why the Buildkite Build step ran `-x buildSearchableOptions`. That is the argument that ended it: fitting into 4 GB meant releases would ship without their search index. GitHub's runners have the memory free on a public repo.

Decommissioned by **deleting the repo webhook**, not the pipeline — org `z8dn`, pipeline `aapv`, cluster `a4da0d9f-be57-4ed3-ac5b-1ccceab79c7b`, queue `default` = `6069f2e4-0dae-42b5-ada6-36a76366d092`. Builds 1–96 and their logs are still in Buildkite; re-adding the webhook URL would revive it.

- `gradleVersion`, since bumped past what #48 set
- `qodana-action@v2026.2` — see [[qodana-gha-action-version]]

Buildkite gotchas, still true if it is ever revisited:

- **Cluster secrets are not in the job environment.** Read with `buildkite-agent secret get KEY`; `$${TOKEN?}` never resolves. A missing secret gives `404 Secret not found`.
- **`export VAR="$(cmd)"` swallows `cmd`'s exit status** — it reports `export`'s own, so 0 even under `set -e`. Build 92 sailed past four failed secret reads with empty values because of this. Assign on one line, `export` on the next. This is a plain bash trap, not Buildkite-specific.
- **`if:` and `branches:` are mutually exclusive** on a step; put the branch restriction in the condition.
- A step skipped by `if:` shows as **`broken`** — filtered out, not failed.
- **`buildkite-agent` is not inside the docker plugin's container** without `mount-buildkite-agent: true`.
- **YAML anchors bind to where they are defined** — deleting the step that holds `&anchor` breaks every `*anchor` elsewhere in the file.
- **Hosted agent instance shape cannot be changed via the REST API**; `PATCH` silently ignores it. Use the web UI. Renaming a pipeline via PATCH does work and preserves the webhook URL.
- **The `bk` CLI keeps its token in the macOS keychain**, so `bk` calls need `dangerouslyDisableSandbox` or every REST call returns 401.

Done. **PR #67** — https://github.com/z8dn/advanced-android-project-view/pull/67 — all GitHub Actions checks green.

**Restored verbatim from `4dd081e^`:** `build.yml` (build/test/verify/releaseDraft), `release.yml` (sign + publish + changelog PR), `run-ui-tests.yml`.

**Removed:** `.buildkite/`, `gradle/ci.properties`, and the `build.gradle.kts` `test` block that only existed to read `testMaxHeapSize` from it. `CLAUDE.md`'s CI section now describes the all-GHA setup and records why Buildkite was tried and dropped.

**Not reverted, deliberately** — `git revert -m 1 4dd081e` would have broken the build. PR #48 bundled three load-bearing changes with the CI move: `platformType = AI` (read by `pluginVerification`), `gradleVersion` (since bumped to 9.7.0), and `qodana-action@v2026.2` (the pairing you proved works).

**Decommissioned:** the Buildkite webhook is deleted, so no further builds fire and no new red checks appear. The `aapv` pipeline and builds 1–96 are still in Buildkite — re-adding the webhook URL revives it. PR #66 closed as superseded, branch kept.

I also corrected my project notes, which claimed CI runs on Buildkite. They now record the reverse: the free tier's 2 vCPU / 4 GB agents are why it didn't work, with build 92 and the `buildSearchableOptions` trade-off as the evidence, plus the three changes not to revert if this ever comes up again.

Two things worth flagging before you merge:

- **`run-ui-tests.yml` is restored with a pre-existing defect.** It calls `runIdeForUiTests`, which IntelliJ Platform Gradle Plugin 2.x renamed to `testIdeUi`, and needs `TestFrameworkType.Starter` + `intellij-ui-test-robot` that `build.gradle.kts` doesn't declare. It's `workflow_dispatch`-only so nothing runs it by accident. This predates the migration and I left it alone as out of scope — say the word if you want it fixed.
- **`## [Unreleased]` in `CHANGELOG.md:5` is still empty**, so the v0.0.10 draft has no notes. Once #67 merges, `build.yml`'s `releaseDraft` job will recreate that draft on `main`; publishing it with an empty body means `release.yml` skips both `patchChangelog` and the changelog PR.
